title: Postgres job queue worker

spec.text: Background worker for the Postgres-backed jobs table. Several workers run at once; each job must be handled by only one of them at a time. A failed job is retried until it has been attempted MAX_ATTEMPTS times in total, then marked 'dead'. Jobs whose worker crashed are picked up again after VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT. A customer must never receive the same invoice email twice.

context: Four worker processes on separate hosts, each with one psycopg connection (autocommit off). Invoice rows have an emailed_at column set by invoices.mark_emailed. email_client.send accepts an optional idempotency_key and the provider drops repeats of the same key. New job kinds are sometimes enqueued by the web app before the workers are redeployed.

files.content:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT = timedelta(minutes=5)
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5


def claim_next(db):
    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            """
            SELECT id, kind, payload, attempts FROM jobs
            WHERE status = 'queued'
               OR (status = 'running' AND locked_at < %s)
            ORDER BY created_at
            LIMIT 1
            """,
            (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT,),
        )
        row = cur.fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        cur.execute(
            "UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', locked_at = now() WHERE id = %s",
            (row[0],),
        )
    db.commit()
    return {"id": row[0], "kind": row[1], "payload": row[2], "attempts": row[3]}


def complete(db, job_id):
    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute("UPDATE jobs SET status = 'done' WHERE id = %s", (job_id,))
    db.commit()


def fail(db, job):
    attempts = job["attempts"] + 1
    status = "dead" if attempts > MAX_ATTEMPTS else "queued"
    with db.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            "UPDATE jobs SET status = %s, attempts = %s, locked_at = NULL WHERE id = %s",
            (status, attempts, job["id"]),
        )
    db.commit()

import logging
import time

from jobs import queue
from jobs.handlers import HANDLERS

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def run_forever(db):
    while True:
        job = queue.claim_next(db)
        if job is None:
            time.sleep(1)
            continue
        handler = HANDLERS[job["kind"]]
        try:
            handler(job["payload"])
            queue.complete(db, job["id"])
        except Exception:
            log.exception("job %s failed", job["id"])
            queue.fail(db, job)
